title: A connected étale finite-Tor lisse complex has one perfect constant value
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\underline R)$ has bounded cohomology, each $H^q(L)$ is locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module values [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(L\otimes_R^L F)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $R$-module sheaf $F$ and $q
otin[a,b]$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Then there is a perfect ring complex $E\in D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and an étale covering $\{V_i	o X\}$ with $L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline E|_{V_i}$. For every geometric point $ ar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $E\simeq L_{ ar x}$.

Moreover, if $W	o X$ is an affine object of the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] that is weakly contractible (evaluation at $W$ takes every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection) [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible], then $(
u_X^*L)|_W\simeq\underline E|_W$, where $
u_X$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Neither $R$ nor its finitely generated modules are required to be finite sets.

source.place: Tag 09BI, lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant; the weakly contractible corollary is the trivialization used in proetale.tex, proof of Tag 09C6, together with the covering-splitting condition of sites.tex Tag 090K.

proof.text: Take a K-flat flat-term representative P of L. The constant ring sheaf in degree zero is K-flat (tensoring with it is the identity); the derived-tensor model identifies L\otimes_R^L\underline R with P\otimes_R\underline R\cong P, by x\otimes r\mapsto rx and inverse x\mapsto x\otimes1. Taking F=\underline R therefore gives H^q(L)=0 off [a,b]. Apply the existing bounded-constant-model lemma on the small étale site: obtain a covering {V_i\to X} and complexes M_i^\bullet of finitely generated R-modules, zero outside [a,b], with L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline{M_i^\bullet}. Discard empty V_i. On a nonempty V_i\times_XV_j choose a geometric point; exact geometric stalks, and the constant-sheaf stalk isomorphism termwise, give M_i^\bullet\simeq M_j^\bullet in D(R). These isomorphisms are R-linear since the constant-stalk maps commute with every scalar endomorphism. If the images of V_i and V_j meet, choose a geometric point above a point of intersection and lifts to both étale schemes; the more precise clause of the cited geometric-lifting lemma gives lifts above the chosen points of both fibres. Thus their fibre product is nonempty. For each derived-isomorphism class M among the M_i, form the union of the images of its V_i. These unions are open by the cited openness theorem, are pairwise disjoint by the overlap argument, and cover X. Nonemptiness and connectedness imply exactly one class occurs. Choose its representative M^\bullet. Each geometric point of X lifts to some V_i, so the same exact-stalk calculation gives M^\bullet\simeq L_{\bar x} for every geometric point \bar x.

source.place: Tag 09BI, lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant; local models from Sites Tag 094G and connectedness grouping in the displayed proof

proof.text: Fix a geometric point \bar x of X (one exists because X is nonempty). Its stalk is the inverse image of the topos point p supplied by the cited topos-point lemma. The constant-stalk isomorphism identifies p^{-1}\underline R with R, so module pullback along p is precisely the exact stalk functor, and Lp^*=p^*. For an arbitrary R-module N in degree zero, apply the Tor hypothesis with F=\underline N. The derived tensor/pullback comparison and the constant-stalk isomorphism give p^*(L\otimes_R^L\underline N)\simeq L_{\bar x}\otimes_R^L N\simeq M^\bullet\otimes_R^L N. Exactness of the stalk functor commutes with cohomology, hence this object vanishes in cohomology off [a,b]. Thus the bounded finite-module complex M^\bullet has Tor amplitude [a,b]. The cited bounded-finite-Tor-perfect theorem gives a complex E of finitely generated projective R-modules, zero outside [a,b], isomorphic to M^\bullet in D(R). Termwise constant presheaves preserve exact sequences, and the cited module sheafification theorem is exact; consequently constant-sheaf construction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces a functor on derived categories. Applying it to E\simeq M^\bullet gives L|_{V_i}\simeq\underline E|_{V_i}. Step 1 also gives E\simeq L_{\bar x} for every geometric point.

proof.text:
Let $W	o X$ be affine and weakly contractible. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] to the comparison morphisms $
u_X$ and $
u_{V_i}$ (each a geometric morphism by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]): it identifies $
u_X^*\underline M$ with $\underline M$, and likewise $
u_{V_i}^*\underline M$ with $\underline M$, naturally in every $R$-module $M$. The exactness in [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] permits termwise application to complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the constant comparison also holds for the perfect complex $E$ from Step 2.

source.place: Tags 0H7J and 00YV, constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text:
For $u:V_i	o X$, use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] for the etale inverse image and clause 1 of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] (the object $V_i	o X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$; the scheme-base-change inverse image is restriction, for sheaves of sets and abelian groups, naturally in the sheaf) for the pro-etale inverse image. Substitute these identifications into [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Its natural isomorphism becomes $(
u_X^*G)|_{V_i}\simeq
u_{V_i}^*(G|_{V_i})$. Naturality with respect to addition and the scalar maps makes it $R$-linear; exact module inverse image induces the same comparison termwise on derived categories. Apply it to the isomorphisms of Step 2, and restrict further to $W	imes_XV_i$, using relocalization and constant restriction. This gives $(
u_X^*L)|_{W	imes_XV_i}\simeq\underline E$ on that slice.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism, comparison square; sites.tex Tag 00XZ, localized restriction

proof.text: The projections $W\times_XV_i\to W$ form an etale covering by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. Since $W$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement] gives a finite refining cover $\{U_j\to W\}_{j=1}^m$ with each $U_j$ affine. Restricting the preceding isomorphisms gives $(\nu_X^*L)|_{U_j}\simeq\underline E|_{U_j}$, because derived restriction is exact and constant restriction is natural in the differentials of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0218, lemma-etale-affine; proetale.tex Tag 09C6, weakly contractible covering passage

proof.text: Put $U=\coprod_{j=1}^mU_j$ with its induced map $q:U\to W$. Each $U_j\to W$ is an etale map of affines, hence its ring map is ind-etale (the constant filtered diagram) and weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Composition with $W\to X$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. The finite-family geometry lemma therefore applies to the affine objects $U_j$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$: their scheme coproduct $U$ is an affine pro-etale object. The scheme-coproduct statement gives its disjoint clopen summands, and [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale] gives that $q$ is etale. For every affine open $T\subset W$, base change gives the etale cover $\{U_j\times_W T\to T\}$. Apply the same affine-refinement lemma to it: finitely many affine opens in these fibre products cover $T$, and they are affine opens in the corresponding $U_j$. Thus $\{U_j\to W\}$ satisfies the covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

source.place: Tag 09A1, lemma-w-contractible-hypercovering, finite-family geometry; morphisms.tex Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize

proof.text: The sheaf map $h_U\to h_W$ is an epimorphism: if two sheaf maps $h_W\rightrightarrows F$ agree after $h_U$, their corresponding sections of $F(W)$ agree on each $U_j$, since each $U_j\to W$ factors through $U$. The sheaf equalizer axiom for the cover $\{U_j\to W\}$ makes these sections equal. Yoneda then makes the two maps equal. By weak contractibility, this epimorphism has a section. Subcanonicity and Yoneda identify that section with a scheme map $s:W\to U$ satisfying $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_W$.

Combine the finitely many isomorphisms on U_j to an isomorphism (\nu_X^*L)|_U\simeq\underline E|_U as follows. For any object T\to U, put T_j=T\times_UU_j. The T_j are disjoint and cover T, so the sheaf condition is F(T)=\prod_{j=1}^m F(T_j); no overlap compatibility remains because all distinct intersections are empty and a module sheaf on the empty object is zero. This identifies module sheaves on the slice over U with the finite product of their categories on the slices over U_j, with restriction and inverse assembly exact. Apply the identification termwise to complexes: differentials, chain maps, homotopies and cohomology are computed on each component. In particular the finite family of roofs representing the local derived isomorphisms assembles to a roof on U, and its quasi-isomorphism legs remain quasi-isomorphisms componentwise. Now restrict this isomorphism along s:W\to U, using exact derived restriction and its relocalization identity. Since q\circ s=id_W, its left-hand object becomes (\nu_X^*L)|_W; constant-restriction naturality identifies the right-hand object with \underline E|_W. This proves the moreover clause, including disconnected W. If W is empty both restrictions are zero, and the same conclusion holds.
